claims.text: The initial material is a Ti–Ni-based high-entropy alloy in a single-phase solid-solution state.
The proposed melting pressure is below 10^-6 Torr.
The proposed post-melting treatment is annealing in a purified argon/hydrogen mixture.
In situ impurity monitoring can verify and help maintain sub-ppm interstitial impurity concentrations during processing.
The proposed annealing regime is 600–800°C for several hours.
Ultra-high-vacuum and purified-atmosphere processing will retain a clean single-phase solid solution.
The intervention will produce a defect-minimized structure.
Minimizing oxygen and nitrogen interstitials prevents deleterious impurity-complex formation.
Minimizing oxygen and nitrogen interstitials prevents phase segregation.
Suppressing impurity complexes and phase segregation maintains intrinsic solid-solution strengthening.
Suppressing impurity complexes and phase segregation delays elevated-temperature softening.
The treated alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than a conventionally processed sample.
The treated alloy will have better elevated-temperature creep resistance than a conventionally processed sample.
Typical impurity levels in conventionally processed Ti–Ni HEAs may promote phase segregation during high-temperature exposure.
Typical impurity levels in conventionally processed Ti–Ni HEAs may promote high-temperature softening.
The intervention is applicable at 600–800°C to Ti–Ni HEAs in which Ti and Ni are primary constituents and interstitial-impurity effects are significant.

contradictions.description: The atmosphere is characterized as inert, but the specified annealing atmosphere contains hydrogen; an Ar/H2 mixture is reducing/reactive rather than strictly inert.
